From: lauren_bishop@redwoodai.com
To: sam@paygrid.com, olivia.chen@paygrid.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com, aditya_rao@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: PayGrid model-fit eval: results + recommended configs (attached)

Sam / Olivia — attached is the initial eval (paygrid_model_eval_results.xlsx) and the prompt set (prompt_sets_v2.jsonl). High-level summary: 

Key findings:
- Baseline (PayGrid proprietary) — accuracy on the 5k sample: 0.952 overall; mean latency p95 = 320ms.
- Open-model candidate A (llama-3-70b quantized + Redwood runtime): overall accuracy 0.941, p95 latency 280ms; cost estimate ~ $0.55 per 1M tokens.
- Open-model candidate B (mpt-30b-instruct + optimized batching): overall accuracy 0.927, p95 latency 240ms; cost estimate ~ $0.32 per 1M tokens.
- Redwood-optimized variant (llama-3-70b + KV-prefix caching + prompt engineering): accuracy 0.949, p95 latency 290ms; cost estimate ~ $0.48 per 1M tokens.

Parity assessment and recommendation:
- Parity threshold you mentioned: within 3% absolute accuracy of your proprietary baseline and no >10% regression on high-risk labels.
- Candidate A is within the 3% window but misses on 1 high-risk label (precision drop of 11% on 'tax-exempt vendor').
- Redwood-optimized variant meets the 3% accuracy target and stays within the high-risk label threshold in our simulated human-eval.

Proposed next steps (decision items):
- Pilot Redwood-optimized variant on a 1-week shadow run for production-like traffic to validate latency and tail behavior.
- Run focused human-eval on the 300-edge-case blind set (we can coordinate graders and provide rubric).
- If pilot shows parity, discuss pilot to paid conversion and Dedicated capacity options.

Files and links:
- Eval spreadsheet with per-label breakdown (attached)
- Human-eval rubric and prompt sets (attached)
- Benchmark run: https://redwood.example.com/evals/paygrid-run-20270114

Notes on quality/regression risks:
- We observed sensitivity to prefix prompts on 'tax-exempt vendor' examples; small prompt adjustments and additional few-shot examples in the prompt set improve precision by ~6 percentage points.
- Quantization edge cases: we recommend the Redwood-optimized config (mixed precision + selective dequant) to avoid regressions on numeric fields.

Let us know if you want us to schedule the shadow run for next Wednesday; happy to kick off the human-eval panel as soon as you confirm the graders.

Thanks — Lauren

From: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com

Adding a couple technical notes from the inference/opt team: 

- Acceptance thresholds we typically bake into parity decisions: overall accuracy within 3% AND any label with >5% business impact (you can define this) must be within 7% absolute of baseline. For PayGrid, based on your SLA ask we recommend tightening the high-risk label threshold to 5% absolute.
- For the shadow run we recommend enabling: continuous KV caching, adaptive batching (target latency SLO 350ms p95), and a monitored fallback policy (route to proprietary baseline on edge failures). This minimizes user impact during pilot.
- I'll own the regression alerting dashboard; once the shadow run starts we'll surface any drift >2% within 24h.

Happy to join the kickoff. If you approve, Lauren — please schedule the shadow run and add a short-ops checklist for the pilot.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Applied ML | Redwood Inference
